data.business_summary: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

articles.content:
Nvidia is still having a solid year, but the company has posted incredibly strong results in its first two quarterly reports and arguably hasn't been rewarded as much as some investors would have expected.

Earlier today, Reuters, citing anonymous sources, reported that Chinese companies, including ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent, have ordered more than 3 million Nvidia Blackwell chips, collectively worth $35 billion.

Here's why that could be great news for the stock. [...] Kress also said that Hopper sales are dilutive to gross margins, so it's positive that the company is able to sell Blackwell chips to Chinese customers.

The even better news for investors is that Nvidia has been providing forward guidance without including potential sales to Chinese companies. On the last quarterly call, Kress said the company is projecting revenue for the third quarter of its fiscal year 2027 to come in around $108 billion, so $35 billion is not an insignificant number. [...] Despite the news, Nvidia's stock only traded marginally higher as of 2:04 p.m. ET today, and the market was broadly in the green. The stock has had some difficulty gaining traction, despite reporting blowout numbers and guidance each quarter so far this year.
